picks.editorial_note: NASA's formal entry into the Genesis Mission — a whole-of-government initiative launched by executive order and now spanning 15+ federal agencies — signals the broadest national-policy commitment to AI-accelerated science in this batch, reshaping how federal research will be funded and coordinated for years.
picks.title: NASA Joins Genesis Mission to Accelerate AI-Driven Discovery - NASA

picks.editorial_note: Berkeley Lab's role leading 13 Genesis Mission projects and partnering on 30+ more makes it the single largest institutional stake in the DOE's flagship AI-for-science program revealed this week, concentrating major federal investment in one place.
picks.title: Berkeley Lab to Lead 13 New Genesis Mission AI Projects

picks.editorial_note: Oak Ridge National Lab leading nine Genesis Mission projects and contributing to 32 others represents another top-tier concentration of DOE AI funding, reinforcing ORNL's position as a national supercomputing and AI hub.
picks.title: Department of Energy selects ORNL to lead nine Genesis Mission projects | ORNL

picks.editorial_note: Sandia's lead role on six Genesis Mission projects plus partnership on 17 more ties together AI, HPC, and quantum computing at a major weapons/energy lab, illustrating how deeply the initiative reaches into national security research infrastructure.
picks.title: Sandia selected to lead six Genesis Mission projects, partner on 17 others

picks.editorial_note: CuspAI's £330 million raise at a £2 billion valuation, with an Imperial College London scientist as Chief Scientific Officer, is a rare startup-scale funding event in this batch and shows academic AI materials expertise translating directly into major private capital.
picks.title: Imperial expert leads science at £2 billion AI materials company CuspAI

picks.editorial_note: NSF's $20 million award to Boston University to help build a national 'cloud lab' network of 20 AI-infused remote-experiment nodes creates shared research infrastructure that will benefit institutions well beyond BU.
picks.title: NSF Awards Boston University $20 Million to Help Create National “Cloud Lab” Network

picks.editorial_note: University of Washington and Carnegie Mellon researchers, working with SLAC, are building an AI-driven data service to unify cosmology data streams — a genuine cross-institutional scientific tool with the potential to accelerate discovery across the field, not just at one lab.
picks.title: UW researchers join national effort to streamline AI-driven cosmology

picks.editorial_note: Berkeley Lab's ModCon consortium is developing self-improving AI foundation models trained on DOE data and facilities — a technically ambitious effort that goes beyond typical grant-funded projects toward a new class of scientific AI infrastructure.
picks.title: Q&A: Accelerating Scientific Discovery with the Genesis Mission’s ModCon

picks.editorial_note: RIKEN's new AGIS program to build generative AI foundation models and AI agents for scientific research marks a major Japanese national push comparable in ambition to the U.S. Genesis Mission, broadening the story beyond U.S. institutions.
picks.title: TRIP Headquarters Advanced General Intelligence for Science Program (AGIS)

picks.editorial_note: USC's selection to lead a national team developing AI models for turbulence prediction — with applications spanning energy and transportation — is a distinctive, high-partnership-score project illustrating tangible real-world engineering impact from the Genesis Mission.
picks.title: USC leads national AI research project to accelerate scientific discovery
